research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "So tell me what you're thinking." Permanent on-screen text: "Her business partner paid me to be the most annoying interior design client ever".
research_analysis.visual_hook: A woman with long brunette hair in a black top stands in a house entryway beside an open front door with wrought iron glass. Letterboxed portrait layout with a sparkling border and the permanent text at the top.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: 47.6 seconds, 7 cuts through different rooms. The person holding the camera plays the client. The designer asks a question or offers an idea, the client answers with a contradiction and ends on the same word, "custom". The designer mostly says "Okay." Two reaction zooms with sting sound effects. Ends on her deadpan stare into the lens under soap-opera music.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: One recurring word does the writing. By the second use the viewer is waiting for it, so each new contradiction is a setup for a word they already know is coming. The professional's restrained 'Okay' is the audience's stand-in.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 1.6M views on an account with a 528.5 median (3,067.6x) and 12.7K followers. The client is never on camera. Catchphrase used six times. Caption invites the trade to share their own stories ("interior designers unite").
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the caption turns the comments into a thread of professionals trading client stories, and people in any service trade swap the word for their own industry's version. The off-camera client means viewers project their own worst client onto the voice.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: It puts Alex on camera reacting, which is what carried his 13.5M Reel, and it is about clients, his one proven business topic. It needs only one friend holding the phone.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: camera-holder plays the client, one buzzword ends every line, professional under-reacts, stare to lens at the end. New: the word is "authentic", the setting is a content shoot, every line is new, and the final beat breaks the pattern: the client rejects the only authentic idea as "fake".

alex_adaptation.concept: A friend holds the camera and plays a client walking Alex through what they want from their videos. Every request is the opposite of authentic and every one ends with the word "authentic". When Alex suggests the client just talk to the camera for ten seconds, the client says that would feel fake.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Marketers, videographers, social media managers and business owners who have used the word 'authentic' in a brief.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Alex walking backwards through a doorway into a business space (or his own place), camera bag on his shoulder, looking at the person holding the phone. Permanent text at top: "I asked my friend to play every client I've ever had, at once".
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: Okay, so what's the vision for the videos?

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: Okay, so what's the vision for the videos?
full_script.action: Open, friendly, professional. Notebook in hand.
full_script.camera: Handheld POV from the collaborator, Alex chest-up, walking.
full_script.on_screen_text: I asked my friend to play every client I've ever had, at once
full_script.editing: Permanent top text all video. Word-by-word captions; the word 'authentic' always in yellow.

full_script.speaker: Client (collaborator, off camera)
full_script.dialogue: I want it real. Raw. Like we didn't plan any of it. So I'll need the full script by Monday. Authentic.
full_script.action: Alex starts writing, stops at 'script by Monday', looks up.
full_script.audio: Client voice close to the mic.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.editing: Cut to a second spot in the space.

full_script.speaker: Client
full_script.dialogue: And I don't want to be on camera. Or my staff. Or the building. But authentic.
full_script.action: Alex looks around the room at everything he is not allowed to film.

full_script.speaker: Client
full_script.editing: Snap zoom to Alex's face on 'Authentically', hold 0.7 seconds.
full_script.audio: One short orchestral sting on the zoom.

full_script.speaker: Client
full_script.dialogue: Could we hire an actor to play me? Someone taller. Authentic.
full_script.action: Alex is now sitting or leaning, rubbing his forehead. He does not look up until 'taller'.

full_script.speaker: Client
full_script.dialogue: And when people comment, I want you to reply as me. Really be me. But don't ask me anything about myself. Authentic.
full_script.action: Alex opens his mouth to ask a question and closes it at 'don't ask me anything'.
full_script.editing: Second snap zoom on 'Authentic', hold 0.7 seconds.
full_script.audio: Second sting, a different one (choir hit).

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: What if you just talk to the camera for ten seconds? Like, right now. As you.
full_script.action: Last attempt. Hopeful. He lifts his own phone toward the client.

full_script.speaker: Client
full_script.dialogue: I hate that. Honestly, that would feel fake.
full_script.action: Alex lowers his phone very slowly.

full_script.speaker: None
full_script.action: Alex turns his head and looks straight into the lens. No expression. Holds it.
full_script.audio: Dramatic soap-style music swell from a royalty-free library.

alex_adaptation.caption: Tell me your industry's version of this word.

production.location: Any real business space a friend can lend for 20 minutes (gym, cafe, office). Fallback: Alex's own place, three different rooms
production.wardrobe: Work-casual, camera bag on shoulder so he reads as the content guy
shot_list: Spot 2: lines 9 to 18s including the first reaction
Spot 3 (seated or leaning): lines 18 to 29s including the second reaction
Spot 3 continued: phone offer, 'fake', stare to lens
production.editor_instructions: The collaborator reads the client lines from a note on Alex's back or just memorises them; record their voice on the filming phone, close to the mic. Use two different royalty-free stings for the two zooms and a third cue for the ending, all from a licensed library, not from the reference. Highlight 'authentic' in yellow every time. Keep Alex's three 'Okay's getting flatter.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: permanent text 'Every client brief I've ever received, in one meeting'
Alternate payoff: 'can it go viral? Authentically.'
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3. Promote at 48h if views are at least 3x the trailing median and comments or shares per 1,000 reached are top quartile; needs a collaborator, so only make sequels if follows per 1,000 beats the solo skits.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same friend, new word: the client who wants everything 'premium' on no budget
Same friend, new word: the client who says 'organic' but means paid
Roles reversed: Alex holds the camera and plays the agency guy who answers every client question with 'the algorithm'

creative_confidence.rationale: The reference is the highest outlier multiple in the comedy set and the mechanism is simple to write. The pattern-break ending gives it a real punchline instead of just a sixth repetition.
uncertainties: Depends on a collaborator who can deliver six lines with a straight voice
The permanent text frames it as a friend playing a composite, which is honest but slightly softer than the reference's 'paid me to be the most annoying client' hook
36 seconds with seven cuts is slower to shoot than the solo skits
